findings.message: The supply caps of the phases add up to 5,300 and the reserve to 300, 5,600 in all, 600 above the maxSupply of 5,000. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Lower the caps of the phases or the reserve until they fit in the max supply, or raise the max supply if the contract and the plan of the collection allow it.
findings.own: adding up the caps of the phases and the reserve against the max supply is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; a contract that stops at its max supply makes the last phase sell out early, and one that does not mints more than the collection promised

findings.message: The allow list of phase allowlist has no merkleRoot, so the contract cannot tell a listed wallet from any other. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.subject: allowlist
findings.fix: Build the merkle tree of the allow list and set its root in the plan before the phase opens; if the contract checks a signature instead of a root, say so in the notes of the phase and keep the finding in the review.
findings.own: asking for a merkle root for each allow list is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the common way to hold an allow list in a contract is the root of a merkle tree of the listed wallets, and a phase with none is open to everyone or to no one

findings.message: Phase holders starts at minute 4,320 and ends at minute 4,320, so it is open for no minute. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.subject: holders
findings.fix: Set the end of the phase after its start, in the timing of the plan.
findings.own: refusing a phase that ends at or before its start is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; such a phase is almost always a start and an end written the wrong way round or copied from another phase

findings.message: The currency of phase holders is SOL, a currency of Solana, but the collection is ERC-721, on an EVM chain. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.subject: holders
findings.fix: Price the phase in a currency of the chain of the collection, or correct the standard.
findings.own: matching the currency of a phase with the chain of the standard is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the tool knows a short list of currencies and leaves the others alone

findings.message: Phase PUBLIC has no currency, such as ETH or SOL.
findings.subject: PUBLIC
findings.fix: Add the field named; docs/inputs.md lists what the plan needs.

findings.message: The name PUBLIC is also the name of the phase at line 8; each phase needs a name of its own.
findings.subject: PUBLIC
findings.fix: Give every phase a name of its own, and list each signer once.

findings.message: The royalty is 1,250 basis points (12.5%) but names no receiver. The royaltyInfo of ERC-2981 answers a marketplace with the address the royalty is sent to, and a royalty with no receiver has nowhere to go.
findings.fix: Name the receiver of the royalty, such as the multisig of the team or a contract that splits it, or set the royalty to 0.

basis.text: The royaltyInfo function of ERC-2981 answers a marketplace with two values for a sale: the address the royalty is to be sent to, and the amount.

findings.message: The placeholderUri of the reveal is "placeholder.json", which is not a URI the tool reads; write ipfs://, ar://, https:// or data: with the rest of the address.
findings.fix: Write the value as docs/inputs.md shows: text for names, addresses and choices, whole numbers for supplies, limits, starts and ends, plain decimal numbers for prices, true or false for flags.

findings.message: The minter of the admin roles, "0x12345", has 5 characters after 0x, not 40; an address of an EVM chain is 0x followed by 40 hex digits. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Copy the address again from the wallet; send nothing to a zero address, which no one holds.
findings.own: checking the form of an address is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the form is the one wallets write on each chain, no page is saved for it, and a typo or a zero address in a plan sends the royalties or the proceeds where no one can reach them

findings.message: The plan holds the key "seedPhrase", which names a seed, a mnemonic or a private key. The tool never reads one, and the value is not shown.
findings.fix: Remove the value from the plan and from wherever the plan was copied, treat it as exposed and move what it controls to a new key. A launch plan names wallets by their public address only.

findings.message: The signer 0x6666666666666666666666666666666666666666 of the multisig is listed twice; it was counted once.
findings.fix: Give every phase a name of its own, and list each signer once.

findings.message: The withdraw address, "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", is the zero address, which no one holds; an address of an EVM chain is 0x followed by 40 hex digits. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Copy the address again from the wallet; send nothing to a zero address, which no one holds.
findings.own: checking the form of an address is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the form is the one wallets write on each chain, no page is saved for it, and a typo or a zero address in a plan sends the royalties or the proceeds where no one can reach them

findings.message: The key "perWalletLimt" of phase 1 is not one the tool reads, so its value was left out of every check. Did you mean "perWalletLimit"? The keys of phase 1 are name, start, end, price, currency, perWalletLimit, supplyCap, allowList, notes.
findings.fix: Correct the spelling to a field of docs/inputs.md, or remove it.

findings.message: The allow list of phase allowlist holds 1,500 wallets, but the phase is capped at 1,000, so some listed wallets may find it sold out. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.subject: allowlist
findings.fix: Raise the supply cap of the phase, lower the per-wallet limit or the size of the list, or tell the listed wallets that a place on the list does not hold a token.
findings.own: comparing the allow list and its per-wallet limit with the cap of the phase is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; many launches list more wallets than the phase holds on purpose, so it is a warning

findings.message: Phase public is open to every wallet and free, with no perWalletLimit, so one wallet, or a set of bots, can mint as much of it as it can pay for. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.subject: public
findings.fix: Set perWalletLimit on every public phase, above all on a free or cheap one, and keep in mind that a limit per wallet does not stop one person with many wallets.
findings.own: asking for a per-wallet limit on a public phase is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the tool cannot know which price is low for a collection, so it reports every public phase with no limit and says when the phase is free

findings.message: Phase public starts at minute 1,200, before phase allowlist ends at minute 1,440, so the two are open together for 240 minutes. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.subject: public
findings.fix: Start each phase when the one before it ends, or say in the plan why two phases share a window.
findings.own: asking for phases that follow one another is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; some launches run two phases at once on purpose, so it is a warning

findings.message: The royalty is 1,250 basis points (12.5%), above the threshold of 1,000 (10%) of --max-royalty-bps. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Check the royalty against what the marketplaces the collection sells on honour and what its buyers expect, or raise --max-royalty-bps for a collection that sets a higher royalty on purpose.
findings.own: warning above a threshold of 10% is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; ERC-2981 sets no limit, and the threshold can be changed with --max-royalty-bps

findings.message: The reveal is delayed and gives no provenanceHash, so collectors cannot check that the order of the art was fixed before the mint. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Hash the final metadata or images in their order, publish the hash before the mint opens and set it in the plan as provenanceHash.
findings.own: asking for a provenance hash before a delayed reveal is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; no cited page asks for one, and without it the team could choose which tokens get which art after seeing who minted them

findings.message: The metadata are never frozen (freeze is never), so the owner can change the art and the traits of every token after the sale. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Plan a freeze, at the mint or after the reveal, that makes the metadata permanent, or say to collectors that the metadata stays open to change and why.
findings.own: asking for a freeze of the metadata is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; some collections change on purpose, so it is a warning

findings.message: The metadata of this ERC-721 collection change after the mint (the reveal is delayed), but the plan does not say that the contract emits the events of ERC-4906 (erc4906 is false). A contract with that extension emits MetadataUpdate or BatchMetadataUpdate when the JSON metadata change, so that marketplaces refresh the tokens.
findings.fix: Add the ERC-4906 extension to the contract, emit BatchMetadataUpdate at the reveal and MetadataUpdate on each later change, and set metadata.erc4906 to true.

basis.text: ERC-4906 is an optional extension of ERC-721 with two events, MetadataUpdate and BatchMetadataUpdate; a contract that has it emits one of them whenever the JSON metadata of a token, or of a run of tokens, changes, so that marketplaces show the new metadata.
The optional metadata extension of ERC-721 gives each token a tokenURI, a URI that may point to a JSON file with the name, the description and the image of the token.

findings.message: The owner of the contract, 0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111, is not the multisig of the plan, so one key can change the contract, its supply, its price and its metadata. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Make the owner and the withdraw address a multisig wallet that needs more than one signer, and set it in admin.multisig.
findings.own: asking for more than one key behind the owner and the proceeds is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the cited pages do not say how a contract is owned

findings.message: The multisig needs only 1 signature of its 2 signers, so any one signer acts alone. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Set the threshold to at least 2, and to a majority of the signers for the owner of the contract.
findings.own: asking for a threshold above 1 is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; a multisig of threshold 1 is as strong as its weakest key

findings.message: The link website, "http://harbor-owls.example", starts with http, which anyone on the way can change; write https. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Write each link as https:// and the host and path of the page; the tool never opens it.
findings.own: asking for https links is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; a plan whose links are written wrong sends collectors to the wrong page on launch day, and an http link can be changed on the way
